title: Onto (Surjective) Functions
quickIdea: Count all functions, then remove those that miss at least one target element - an inclusion-exclusion over the missed elements.
remember: All functions from an m-set to an n-set: n^m.
Onto: sum over k of (-1)^k C(n,k) (n-k)^m, which equals n! S(m,n).
Onto is impossible when m < n.
One-to-one from an m-set to an n-set: P(n,m).

example.prompt: Onto functions from a 5-element set to a 3-element set.

gateAngle: Two independent methods (inclusion-exclusion and Stirling) must agree - that agreement is the fastest self-check available in the exam.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many onto functions from a 4-element set to a 2-element set?

trap.what: Forgetting the alternating signs when more than two targets can be missed.
trap.why: With three targets, functions missing one target are subtracted three times, then functions missing two targets must be added back.
trap.counterexample: 3^5 - 3 x 2^5 = 147 is not the onto count; the +3 correction gives 150.

check.question: How many onto functions are there from a 3-element set to a 2-element set?
